note: Centre Yanbu; covers Yanbu al-Bahr, Yanbu Industrial City, Badr and Yanbu Airport (YNB). Coastal; shared edges with Umluj, Medina and Rabigh.
Centre Umluj; covers the town and the southern Red Sea Project resorts 60-100 km to the north (8 hotels). Coastal, with offshore islands near the shore; edges with Yanbu and Al-`Ula.
Centre Turaif; covers the town and Turaif Airport (TUI). The north edge follows the Jordan and Iraq borders; edges with Qurayyat and Tubarjal.

Centre Tabuk; covers the city and Prince Sultan Airport (TUU). A 103 km circle cut by the Jordan border to the north-west; the Red Sea coast and NEOM sites (Haql, Sharma, Duba) lie beyond it and have hotels in no city.

p_note: 78,354 stands (GeoNames town 40,019; the figure likely includes the governorate)
note: Centre Tubarjal; covers the town and the Wadi as-Sirhan farms; no airport, no hotels. Shares edges with Qurayyat, Turaif and Sakakah.

Centre Sakakah; covers the Al Jawf depression with Dumat al-Jandal 40 km south-west and Al Jouf Airport (AJF). South of about 29.6 N the circle ran 40 km into the Great Nafud dunes with no place, hotel or road; that part is now in no city. Shares edges with Tubarjal and Arar.

p_note: 72,086 stands; GeoNames Sabya 228,375 probably the governorate
note: Centre Sabya; covers Damad, Az Zabyah, Ash Shuqayri and Ash-Shaqiq on the coast. Tihama plain between Jizan to the south, Khamis Mushait (the Asir escarpment) to the north-east and the Yemen border. The north edge now dips south of Ad Darb, which goes whole to Khamis Mushait.

Centre Rabigh; covers the town, the refinery and King Abdullah Economic City (KAEC) with its Haramain station and Bay La Sun hotels. Thuwal and KAUST are Jeddah's by Colin's ruling; the shared edge runs at 22.345 N. Coastal water to the west; Yanbu, Medina, Mecca and Ta'if around it.
Centre Bisha; covers Wadi Bisha, Tabalah and Bisha Airport (BHH). On the plateau east of the Asir; straight edges with Al Bahah to the west and Khamis Mushait to the south.

Centre Najran; covers the Najran valley, Al Mash'iliyah, Habuna and Najran Airport (EAM). The south edge is the Yemen border (closed); the east edge reaches the western margin of the Rub' al Khali along the Sharurah road, left as it is (highway, not dunes).

p_note: GASTAT 2022 census, as listed in Wikipedia 'List of cities and towns in Saudi Arabia' (ranked table, oldid 1374223212): 2,385,509 (both tables agree); old 1,578,722 is 0.66 of it; p updated (Colin 2026-10-14: a census major correction is enough)
note: Centre the Masjid al-Haram; covers Al Jumum, Mina, Arafat and Muzdalifah; no airport of its own (JED serves it). Straight shared edges with Jeddah to the west and Ta'if to the east, the Ta'if edge near the foot of the Hejaz escarpment at Al-Hada. The Haramain high-speed line to Jeddah and Medina is intercity and did not shape the outline.

p_note: 387,553 is Khamis Mushait alone; the area meant includes Abha (GeoNames 210,886); consider about 600,000+
note: Centre Khamis Mushait; covers Abha, the Abha-Khamis corridor and Abha International Airport (AHB). Shapes: the Asir escarpment to the west (the Muhayil hotels below it at 70 km stay, no better city), Sabya and Jizan in the Tihama to the south-west, Najran and Bishah to the east. Ad Darb, at the foot of the Shaar pass road to Abha, was split by the Sabya line and now goes whole to Khamis Mushait.

p_note: 105,198 stands (city proper; Jazan region far larger)
note: Centre Jizan; covers Abu Arish, Samtah and King Abdullah Airport (GIZ). Coastal Tihama; the Yemen border (closed) to the south-east and Sabya to the north. The Farasan Islands lie offshore outside it.

p_note: GASTAT 2022 census city 3.75 M (Wikipedia list of Saudi cities); 4,697,000 is higher than the census but within metro definitions, figure stands
note: Centre Al-Balad; covers the coastal city from the south corniche to Obhur, King Abdulaziz International Airport (JED), and Thuwal with KAUST 80-90 km north on the direct coastal road (Colin, 2026-10-14: KAUST belongs to Jeddah although the influence rule gives Rabigh 690 against Jeddah 531). The east edge is a straight shared line with Mecca at about 39.5-39.6 E; the Rabigh edge runs at 22.345 N, between KAUST and King Abdullah Economic City; the west edge runs out into the Red Sea with a few points.

Centre Ha'il; covers the city between the Aja and Salma ranges and Ha'il Airport (HAS). A full 103 km circle; its north rim touches the southern margin of the Great Nafud, and Jubbah lies just inside on that side.

Centre Hafar Al-Batin; covers King Faisal Military City, Qaisumah and Al Qaisumah Airport (AQI). The north edge follows the Kuwait and Iraq borders; Kuwait City, KW, reworked 2026-10-14, is not touched.

Centre Buraydah; covers Unaizah, Ar Rass, Al Bukayriyah, Al Badai and Qassim Airport (ELQ). A full 103 km circle on the Qassim plain; it also takes Az Zulfi (84 km, beyond the Nafud ath Thuwayrat sand belt), which has no nearer city; left for Colin rather than cut.

Centre Ta'if; covers Al-Hada and Ash Shafa on the escarpment rim and Ta'if Airport (TIF). The west edge, shared with Mecca, follows the Hejaz escarpment; south-east it runs over the plateau towards Turabah and meets Al Bahah.

Centre As Sulayyil; covers the town and, 70-80 km west, Wadi ad-Dawasir (Al Khamasin), which holds all 8 of its hotels and the Wadi al-Dawasir airport. The south-east part of the circle lay in the Rub' al Khali sands with no place, hotel or road and is now in no city; the Najran road to the south-west is kept. Colin may prefer the city named after Wadi ad-Dawasir.

p_note: GASTAT 2022 census, as listed in Wikipedia 'List of cities and towns in Saudi Arabia' (ranked table, oldid 1374223212): 7,000,100 (the same page's summary table says 7,009,100); old 4,205,961 is 0.60 of it; p updated (Colin 2026-10-14: a census major correction is enough)
note: Centre Al-Batha/Olaya; covers Diriyah, Irqah, Al Uyaynah and King Khalid International Airport (RUH) 35 km north. A near full 103 km circle except the south-east, where it shares a straight edge with Al Kharj; Riyadh Metro and the ring roads sit well inside. Hotels along the Qassim road at Shaqra and Al Majma'ah lie beyond it in no city.
Centre Arar; covers the city and Arar Airport (RAE). The north edge follows the Iraq border; shares a long edge with Sakakah to the south-west.
Centre Qurayyat; covers the city and Gurayat Airport (URY). A small triangle bounded by the Jordan border and edges with Turaif and Tubarjal.
Centre AlUla; covers the old town, Hegra and AlUla International Airport (ULH). A 103 km circle in the Hejaz highlands, with edges shared with Tabuk and Umluj.

p_note: GASTAT 2022 census 1.41-1.48 M; 1,300,000 stands (GeoNames Sultanah 946,697 is a district of Medina)
note: Centre the Prophet's Mosque; covers the city and Prince Mohammad bin Abdulaziz Airport (MED). A 103 km circle over the Hejaz plateau, cut by shared edges with Yanbu to the west and Rabigh to the south-west. One hotel disc at 40.51 E, 24.87 N sits on the outer edge; harmless.
Centre Al Kharj (As Sih); covers Ad Dilam, Al Hayathim and Hawtah Bani Tamim to the south; Prince Sultan Air Base is military, no civil airport. Shares a straight edge with Riyadh to the north-west.
Centre Al Khafji; covers the town and As Saffaniyah. The north edge is the Kuwait border, shared with Kuwait City, KW (not touched); the Gulf to the east and Al Jubayl to the south.

Centre Jubail; covers the old town and Jubail Industrial City. Coast and Gulf water to the east, Al Khafji to the north and Dammam to the south; Safwa and Tarut fall on the Dammam side and no town is cut.

p_note: 729,606 stands; after the merge it should be read as the Al-Ahsa pair (GeoNames Hofuf 293,179 + Mubarraz 290,802); recheck against GASTAT 2022
note: Centre Hofuf; now covers the whole Al-Ahsa oasis: Hofuf, Al Mubarraz, the eastern villages (Al Jafr, Al Qarah, Al Munayzilah), Abqaiq 60 km north and Al-Ahsa International Airport (HOF). Al Mubarraz, SA was a separate city whose centre sat 8 km from Hofuf's, with the shared line running through Al Mubarraz itself; the two discs overlap, so no line could avoid cutting a town, and the pair is merged. South it covers the Ghawar oilfield strip (Udhailiyah); east the Jafurah sands to the Qatar border.

p_note: 88,419 stands; GeoNames Sabt Alalayah 100,000 looks inflated
note: Centre Al Bahah; covers Baljurashi, Al Mindak, Al Aqiq with Al-Baha Airport (ABT), and the Tihama below the escarpment to the coast. Straight edge with Bisha to the east (Sabt Alalayah is 4.6 km clear of it), Ta'if to the north and Khamis Mushait to the south.
Centre Afif; covers the town on the Riyadh-Ta'if road. A 103 km circle on empty Najd plateau, with an edge shared with Ad Dawadimi.
Centre Ad Dawadimi; covers the town, Sajir and Dawadmi Airport. A 103 km circle on the Najd plateau along the Riyadh-Ta'if road, sharing edges with Buraydah and Afif.

p_note: GASTAT 2022 census, as listed in Wikipedia 'List of cities and towns in Saudi Arabia' (ranked table, oldid 1374223212): 1,386,671 for Dammam city (Khobar 409,549 and Dhahran 143,936 counted apart); old 768,602 is 0.55 of it; supersedes the GeoNames 1,252,523 proposed earlier; p updated (Colin 2026-10-14: a census major correction is enough)
note: Centre Dammam; covers Khobar, Dhahran, Qatif, Tarut, Saihat, Thuqbah and King Fahd International Airport (DMM). Shapes: the Gulf coast, the shared water edge with Manama, BH across the King Fahd Causeway (a closed border), Al Jubayl to the north and Al Hufuf (formerly Al Mubarraz) to the south-west. The Dammam-Khobar corridor is intra-city and lies wholly inside.
